subject: Clarify archive / snapshot purge timeline and log retention windows
messages:
From: Lisa Monroe <lisa.monroe@medisys.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2027 10:15:00 -0400
Subject: Archive/snapshot purge timeline — clarifications for SIG questionnaire

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for taking the time on Friday. We are working through the SIG / SIG-lite pack for our security review and a couple of items around logs and backups need exact timings so our DPO can sign off. Can you confirm the following as precisely as possible?

- Retention window for production request logs (API request metadata, not prompt/response payload) — are these retained 90 days or 180 days by default for Hosted customers?
- Snapshot/backup lifecycle: how long are nightly snapshots kept before permanent deletion from the backup store? Is there a point-in-time archive longer than the standard snapshot TTL?
- Prompt retention: do you keep any prompt text outside of ephemeral KV caches, e.g., in any analytics or debug traces? If so, please state the default retention and whether it is masked/hashed.
- Deletion proof: for customers who request data erasure under DPA, what artifacts can you provide to prove deletion of logs/snapshots (timestamps, S3 object delete markers, WORM audit entries)?

If you have a one-pager or a matrix we can attach to the SIG response that lists default vs. configurable retention and the deletion evidence types, that would be ideal. Our compliance team is on a tight timeline and needs this by Wednesday EOD.

Appreciate it — Lisa

--
Lisa Monroe
Head of Compliance
MediSys Health
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Monroe <lisa.monroe@medisys.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2027 12:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Archive/snapshot purge timeline — clarifications for SIG questionnaire

Hi Lisa — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Neha (Security) and Aditya (Account lead) so we can give you authoritative language and artifacts. Quick answers up front while we assemble attachments:

- Production request logs: Hosted customers default to 90 days for request metadata; we offer configurable retention up to 365 days on Dedicated plans or via a contract addendum.
- Snapshots/backups: nightly snapshots are retained 30 days by default in the primary backup tier; we offer long-term point-in-time archive (90/180/365 days) as an opt-in retention tier.
- Prompt retention: we do not persist prompt text in analytics by default. Prompts may be stored transiently in encrypted KV cache for up to 1 hour for active sessions; debug traces that contain prompt text are kept only if the customer enables enhanced logging and then only for a configurable period (default 7 days).
- Deletion proof: we can provide S3 object delete markers and a signed deletion time window report, plus an audit log extract showing the deletion event and the request id. For Dedicated/Private customers we can additionally provide backup manifest snapshots showing object-level tombstones.

I'll have Neha attach a succinct retention matrix and a short policy excerpt you can include in the SIG response. Aditya — should we include the DPA amendment draft as well for MSH to sign?

Vanessa

--
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Lisa Monroe <lisa.monroe@medisys.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Aug 2027 09:30:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Archive/snapshot purge timeline — clarifications for SIG questionnaire

Lisa / team — attaching the retention matrix and short artifacts per Vanessa's note. Highlights and suggested SIG language below. Attachments: redwood_logs_retention_matrix.csv, backup-snapshot-policy.pdf, dpa-amendment-draft.docx (draft).

Suggested concise wording for SIG: 
"Redwood Inference retains production request metadata by default for 90 days for Hosted customers. Customers on Dedicated or under contract can configure retention up to 365 days. Nightly backups are retained 30 days in the primary backup tier; customers may opt into point-in-time archival for longer retention (90/180/365 days) via configuration or contractual amendment. Prompt text is not persisted to analytics by default; transient KV cache retention is ≤1 hour. Debug traces containing prompt content are only stored if a customer enables enhanced logging and may be configured (default 7 days). For DPA erasure requests we provide deletion artifacts including S3 object delete markers, signed deletion reports with timestamps, and audit log extracts referencing the deletion request id. For Dedicated/Private deployments, we can produce backup manifests that demonstrate object tombstones and retention transitions."

Notes: (1) For customers requiring HIPAA-compatible policies, include the backup manifest option in the DPA and confirm encryption-at-rest + KMS key rotation policies. (2) If MediSys wants deletion proof that includes a WORM retention proof, we will need a short SOW to enable extended immutability audit logs.

Happy to convert the suggested wording into a single-page PDF if that helps the SIG response.

Neha

--
Neha Kapoor
Security & Privacy Lead
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_logs_retention_matrix.csv (table of default vs configurable retention), backup-snapshot-policy.pdf (excerpts of backup lifecycle), dpa-amendment-draft.docx (DPA language for archival options)

Neha / Vanessa — this is perfect, thank you. The suggested language reads well and the attachments will slot directly into our SIG responses. A couple of small follow-ups from our DPO: if we opt into 365-day archive we need to confirm whether those archives are automatically included in deletion requests or if a separate archival purge must be requested. Also, can you confirm the format of the signed deletion report (CSV? PDF with signed timestamp?). If you can update the DPA draft to explicitly state that archives are included in erasure by default unless an opt-out is executed, that will speed approvals.

If you can send a one-page PDF with the suggested SIG wording plus a sample signed deletion report (redacted) by EOD Thursday that would close this loop for us.

Best,
Lisa
